name: Dark Maroon Purple
lede: Dark Maroon Purple is a greyed, dark purplish red that ColorHub's library carries as an English rendering of Budōnezumi, a traditional Japanese name meaning "grape mouse."

sections.title: A grape, greyed like a mouse
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Budōnezumi (葡萄鼠), literally "grape mouse": budō names the dark reddish purple of a grape, and nezumi ("mouse") marks it as a muted, greyed version of that hue [1]. The same swatch independently turns up in Ridgway's 1912 standard, plate XXVI, hue 71′, tone m, an aged plate scan read as approximate [2]. Ridgway also carries a near-duplicate, Dark Livid Purple, only 2.3 units away on plate XXXVII [2].

The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places it in block 242, "dark reddish purple," about 5.4 units from that block's centre [3]. Our library's nearest other named color is [[eggplant]], 3.1 units away, a close but distinct purple [3]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 32, chroma 16, hue close to pure red (359°) [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 61 of 23,781 paintings, about a quarter of one percent, as photographed [4]. The earliest match is Ambrogio Lorenzetti's *St. John the Baptist*, from 1337, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. It is nearly always a shadow or a mid-tone (46 and 49 percent of its occurrences) and almost never a highlight, which fits a dark, desaturated hue [4]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[umber]] and [[taupe]] [4]. [[painter:john-singer-sargent|John Singer Sargent]]'s work carries it at four times the archive's overall rate, though only in three of his paintings [4].
